What the test would need for -0.010 at 28/20/52: honest class-2/3 gains add +0.0048; a rank 1 -> 2 flip of a correct answer costs 0.5, so class 1 alone would need a flip rate of 10.6%, classes 1+2 together 6.2%, or 4.2% if the test's class-3 gain is zero. Bench rates: see the re-ordering table (correct answer loses rank 1).

Kernel means for class 1/2 proxies by V22 position: 1: -0.0063, 2-3: -0.0261, 4-10: -0.0047, 11-25: -0.0089

## Reading (19 Oct run; re-check the numbers above if the inputs change)

- **No bench, and no class mix, reproduces the LB.** np: rel250 is a gain at every mix (its class 2 is memorised) and gen20 is a loss only when class 3 is < ~6% of the test. unseen: rel100 and gen20 are gains at every mix. honest (np class 1 + unseen class 2/3): all four signs come out right only for mixes with >= 56% class 1 and <= 30% class 3, none of which is level-plausible (V22 would score >= 0.54 there, not 0.451), and even the best of those mixes gets all signs right in only 43% of bootstrap draws (14% among level-plausible mixes).
- **gen20 vs the honest bench:** +0.004 [-0.001, +0.011] at 28/20/52; LB -0.010 is a ~1% tail of the 124-molecule simulation. Either the test has a property the bench lacks, or the LB draw was unlucky (1 molecule at rank 1 = 0.008).
- **Mechanism seen on the bench:** gen20 hardly crowds (no new candidate ever takes rank 1 on class 1/2) but it re-scores the candidates V22 already had: engine 1 features are list-relative (rank_norm, z, gap-to-max, softmax, formula_share; fragment scoring capped at frag_max_cand=600), so adding up to 350 generated candidates reorders the top 5 in ~50-60% of molecules and moved the correct class-1 answer off rank 1 in 2/70 engine-1 lists (1/70 after fusion).
- **Why the bench is blind to it:** bench answers have ~180 library spectra each vs a median of 6 for training structures, so class-1/2 answers win by margins a re-scoring rarely overturns, while class-3 gains are leak-inflated (engine-1 models saw those structures). The test needs a correct-answer flip rate of ~4-11% (table above) for -0.010.
- **Minimal bench fix:** a "thin class 1" slice: class-1 molecules keep only 1-5 of their other library spectra (match the training n_spec distribution), scored with the engine-1 lists (CPU, like gensweep). Gate generation and list-composition changes on the correct-answer rank-1 loss rate on that slice; it predicts gen20 negative if the rate reaches ~4%+. Unverified until that slice is run.
